explanation: The Soviet war’s lead runs straight into the civil war of 1992: the support that stopped in 1991 is what the government fell without. The article reads: "Following the dissolution of the Soviet Union in December 1991, all support to the Democratic Republic was stopped, leading to the toppling of the government by the mujahideen in 1992 and the start of a second Afghan Civil War (1992–1996)."
